analysis.summary: England topped Group L with six goals scored in three games and will enter this Round of 32 fixture as strong favourites against a DR Congo side making their debut knockout-stage appearance. DR Congo qualified as one of the best third-place teams after drawing Portugal 1-1, losing narrowly to Colombia, and beating Uzbekistan 3-1, showing both counter-attack threat and defensive discipline. England's ability to break down deep defensive blocks is the key question — they were held 0-0 by Ghana in the group stage — while DR Congo's pace on the break makes a clean sheet far from guaranteed. The talent gap is substantial but the tactical matchup suits the underdog.
analysis.home_form: England won Group L with 7 points (W2 D1), beating Croatia 4-2 in their opener, drawing 0-0 with Ghana in a game where they struggled against a low block, then defeating Panama 2-0. Harry Kane scored three times in the group stage; Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka (returned from Achilles issue vs Panama) are also key contributors. England have averaged 2.0 goals per game and conceded 2 in 3 matches.
analysis.away_form: DR Congo finished third in Group K with 4 points (W1 D1 L1): drew 1-1 with Portugal, lost 0-1 to Colombia, then beat Uzbekistan 3-1 to advance. They scored 4 goals and conceded 2 across three games. Yoane Wissa (Brentford) and Cedric Bakambu are the main attacking threats; Chancel Mbemba leads the defence with 107 caps. The Leopards rely on a disciplined low block and lethal counter-attacks, as demonstrated by holding Portugal to a draw.
analysis.h2h: England and DR Congo have no prior competitive or recorded international meetings — this is the first-ever encounter between the two nations.
injuries_news: England: Reece James (hamstring) ruled out of this match.
England: Jarell Quansah (twisted ankle, sustained vs Panama) ruled out of this match.
England: Tino Livramento (calf) was already absent from the squad before the tournament; Trevoh Chalobah called up as replacement.
England: Djed Spence expected to fill in at right-back.
DR Congo: Rocky Bushiri (injury) missed the tournament; Aaron Tshibola called up late. No other confirmed injuries reported for this fixture.
key_factors: England's right-back position is weakened by the absences of James and Quansah — Wissa's pace and DR Congo's counter-attack down that flank is a genuine threat.
England were held scoreless by Ghana's low block (0-0) in the group stage; DR Congo are likely to deploy an even more disciplined 5-4-1 or 4-5-1 defensive shape.
DR Congo drew Portugal 1-1 — Portugal are a higher-ranked side than England — demonstrating their defensive capacity at this level.
Kane, Bellingham and Saka provide elite quality to unlock a packed defence through individual moments and set pieces.
Atlanta venue: July heat and humidity could favour a lower-tempo match and could slightly help DR Congo's game plan of absorbing pressure.
Tournament context: England must win in 90 or ET (no draw possible in knockout stage); extra time available if needed adds 30 minutes of fatigue.
DR Congo are playing at their debut knockout stage with high motivation but relatively little experience of high-pressure elimination football.

value_notes: Market-implied probabilities (overround removed, draw zeroed for knockout): England win ~91%, DR Congo win ~9%. My model sits at England 83% / DR Congo 17% — I give DR Congo a meaningful edge on the counter given England's low-block struggles (Ghana 0-0) and right-back injuries exposing space for Wissa; the market may underweight this given raw rankings. No edge flagged on England (market is tighter than my estimate, not wider). On totals, market implies 50% over 2.5 (odds 2.00); my model puts it at 45% — DR Congo's defensive structure makes sub-3-goal games likely, but the edge on under is only ~5%, borderline. On btts: market implies 37.3% (odds 2.68); my model puts BTTS-yes at ~30%, meaning btts_no at ~70% vs market-implied 69% — negligible edge. No selection clears the 0.05 edge threshold cleanly on the goal markets. The only potential value identification: DR Congo to advance at 13.00 (implied 7.4%) vs my 17% estimate gives an edge of ~0.096, which exceeds the 0.05 threshold — ticket-builder should consider DR Congo h2h away at 13.00.
